question: Should a requester’s proven consumption of descendant output permanently count as `delivered` even when the requester’s subsequent outward delivery fails?
rationale: The implementation deliberately changes lifecycle semantics, not only retry mechanics: cleanup and persisted status will treat requester consumption as completed delivery proof.

options.title: Accept requester consumption as delivery
options.body: Approve the narrow contract and require a redacted runtime proof of the consumed-output and failed-final-send path before merge.

options.title: Keep outward delivery as the only delivery proof
options.body: Do not merge this semantic change; retain requester consumption only as diagnostic metadata or redesign it as a separate settled state.

recommendation.title: Accept requester consumption as delivery
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow contract and require a redacted runtime proof of the consumed-output and failed-final-send path before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged lifecycle work and the current patch place this contributor closest to the concrete requester/descendant settlement boundary.
